titulo_es: Causative with have and get (having something done)
descripcion_es: Have/get something done (asking someone else to do something for you); get someone to do, have someone do.
resumen: Have/get + object + past participle shows that another person does something for us (usually because we arrange or pay for it). It is also used to talk about something bad that happened to us: I had my phone stolen.

filas: I'm having my hair cut tomorrow.
asking or instructing someone to do something
I'll have my assistant call you.
persuading or managing to make someone do something
I got my brother to help me move.
something negative that happens to you
She had her bag stolen on the train.

explicacion.texto: Where Spanish says “me corté el pelo” (even if the hairdresser did it), English makes a distinction: I cut my hair (myself) versus I had my hair cut (at the hairdresser's).
Have is conjugated in all tenses: I'm having, I had, I've had, I'll have, I need to have… Questions and negatives use do: Did you have the car serviced?

items: Fixed order: have + OBJECT + past participle (not “have cut my hair”).
Get someone TO do (with to); have someone DO (without to).
You can add by + person: We had the house painted by a local firm.

ejemplos.frase: I need to have my eyes tested.
They're having a swimming pool built in the garden.
ejemplos.traduccion: Se están haciendo una piscina en el jardín.

ejemplos.frase: Where did you get your suit made?
He had his licence taken away for speeding.
ejemplos.traduccion: Le retiraron el carné por exceso de velocidad.

ejemplos.frase: I'll have the receptionist book you a taxi.
ejemplos.traduccion: Le pediré a la recepcionista que le reserve un taxi.

ejemplos.frase: Can you get your sister to pick us up?
ejemplos.traduccion: ¿Puedes conseguir que tu hermana nos recoja?

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I cut my hair at the hairdresser's yesterday.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I had my hair cut at the hairdresser's yesterday.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: If another person does it, use the causative structure.
The object goes between have and the past participle; otherwise it is a past perfect with a different meaning.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I got him fix the tap.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I got him to fix the tap.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with have/get + object + past participle.
ejercicios.frase: My watch is broken. I must ___ (it / repair).
respuestas: have it repaired
get it repaired
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the main structure in the table: have/get + object + past participle to arrange a service. The clue is “My watch is broken” and “I must”: the person is not going to repair it themselves, but will take it to a watchmaker. After “must” comes the infinitive “have” (or “get”), then the object “it” and the past participle “repaired”. Both forms are fine because the card presents get as a more informal variant.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Have/get + object + past participle to arrange a service.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mi reloj está roto. Tengo que llevarlo a arreglar.

errores_previstos.respuesta: repair it
errores_previstos.explicacion: It would mean you are going to repair it yourself; to arrange it you need have/get + object + past participle.

errores_previstos.respuesta: have repaired it
errores_previstos.explicacion: The order is fixed: the object goes before the past participle, “have it repaired”. “Have repaired” would be a perfect tense.

errores_previstos.respuesta: have it repair
errores_previstos.explicacion: After the object comes the past participle “repaired”, not the infinitive.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the causative form in the past.
ejercicios.frase: We ___ (the kitchen / paint) last month. It looks great.
respuestas: had the kitchen painted
got the kitchen painted
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the structure have/get + object + past participle, conjugating have in the tense required, as the card explains. The clue is “last month”, which calls for the past simple: “had” (or “got”). Then comes the object “the kitchen” and the past participle “painted”. In Spanish you say “pintamos la cocina” even if a professional painted it; in English “we painted the kitchen” would mean you did it yourselves.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Past simple of have/get + object + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: El mes pasado nos pintaron la cocina. Ha quedado genial.

errores_previstos.respuesta: painted the kitchen
errores_previstos.explicacion: It would mean you painted it yourselves; for a service you need “had the kitchen painted”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: had painted the kitchen
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is another tense (past perfect: “we had painted”); in the causative the object goes between had and the past participle.

errores_previstos.respuesta: had the kitchen paint
errores_previstos.explicacion: After the object comes the past participle “painted”, not the infinitive.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the causative form in the present continuous.
ejercicios.frase: I can't drive you; I ___ (my car / service) this week.
respuestas: am having my car serviced
'm having my car serviced
am getting my car serviced
'm getting my car serviced
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule on the card that have is conjugated in all tenses and the rest of the structure does not change. The clue is “this week” and the instructions, which ask for the present continuous for a plan already arranged: “am having” (or “'m having”), and also “am getting”. After that come the object “my car” and the past participle “serviced”. “To service a car” is to give it its regular check.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The verb have/get goes in the tense required; the rest does not change.
ejercicios.traduccion: No puedo llevarte en coche: esta semana tengo el coche en el taller para la revisión.

errores_previstos.respuesta: am servicing my car
errores_previstos.explicacion: It would mean you service it yourself; arranging a service requires have/get + object + past participle.

errores_previstos.respuesta: am having serviced my car
errores_previstos.explicacion: The object “my car” goes before the past participle: “am having my car serviced”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: have my car serviced
errores_previstos.explicacion: The instructions ask for the present continuous for a plan this week: “am having”.

glosario.significado: hacer la revisión a un coche

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb.
ejercicios.frase: I finally got the landlord ___ (replace) the old windows.
respuestas: to replace
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the variant with a person from the table: get + person + to + infinitive, which means persuading or managing to make someone do something. The clue is “got the landlord”, with get and a person as the object, and “finally”, which suggests an effort to persuade him. With get, the person is followed by “to”: “to replace”. With have, on the other hand, there would be no to.
ejercicios.traduccion: Por fin conseguí que el casero cambiara las ventanas viejas.

errores_previstos.respuesta: replace
errores_previstos.explicacion: Without “to” is only used with have (“have someone do”); with get you need “to replace”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: replaced
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past participle is used when the object is a thing; here the object is a person who carries out the action: “to replace”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: replacing
errores_previstos.explicacion: “Get someone doing” means getting someone started on doing something continuously; to make them do it you use “to replace”.

ejercicios.frase: The manager had his secretary ___ the documents.
respuestas: send
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the variant from the table have + person + bare infinitive, for asking someone to do something. The clue is “had his secretary”: the verb is have and the object is a person who carries out the action. That is why the base form “send” follows, without to. The list on the card sums it up: have someone DO, get someone TO do.
ejercicios.traduccion: El director hizo que su secretaria enviara los documentos.

por_opcion.to send: Incorrect: “to” belongs with get (“got his secretary to send”), not with have.
por_opcion.sent: Incorrect: the past participle is used when the object is a thing (“had the documents sent”); here the object is the secretary, who does the action.
por_opcion.sending: Incorrect: “have someone sending” is not the structure for giving an instruction; use the base form.

ejercicios.frase: Tom ___ while he was travelling in Peru.
respuestas: had his camera stolen
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the second use on the card: have + object + past participle to talk about something negative that happens to someone, without them arranging it. The clue is “stolen” and the context of a trip: Tom was the victim of a theft. Hence “had his camera stolen”. Spanish uses “le robaron la cámara”, with an impersonal subject; English makes the victim the subject.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Have + object + past participle also expresses something negative that happens to someone.
ejercicios.traduccion: A Tom le robaron la cámara mientras viajaba por Perú.

por_opcion.had his camera stolen: Correct: have + object + past participle for a negative experience.
por_opcion.stole his camera: Incorrect: it would mean Tom stole his own camera.
por_opcion.had stolen his camera: Incorrect: it is the past perfect; once again Tom would be the thief.

opciones: check your teeth by the dentist
respuestas: have your teeth checked
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the fixed-order rule on the card: have + object + past participle, never have + past participle + object. The clue is that the dentist is the one who checks the teeth, so you need the causative, and since the question has “do you”, have is in the base form. Hence “have your teeth checked”. It is the same case as going to the hairdresser's: “have your hair cut”.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¿Cada cuánto te haces una revisión de los dientes?

por_opcion.have your teeth checked: Correct: have + object + past participle, in the fixed order.
por_opcion.have checked your teeth: Incorrect: the object must go before the past participle; also, “have checked” is confused with a perfect tense.
por_opcion.check your teeth by the dentist: Incorrect: “check your teeth” says you check them yourself; “by the dentist” can only be added to a causative or passive structure.

ejercicios.frase: I'm going to have cut my hair on Saturday.
respuestas: I'm going to have my hair cut on Saturday.
I am going to have my hair cut on Saturday.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the fixed-order rule on the card: have + OBJECT + past participle. The clue is “have cut my hair”, where the past participle comes before the object, which turns the structure into something different. The correct sentence is “I'm going to have my hair cut on Saturday”, with “my hair” between “have” and “cut”. The uncontracted form “I am going to” is also fine.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The object goes before the past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: El sábado voy a cortarme el pelo (en la peluquería).

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'm going to have cut my hair on Saturday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: the object “my hair” has to go before the past participle.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'm going to cut my hair on Saturday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It would mean you are going to cut it yourself; arranging it requires “have my hair cut”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'm going to have my hair cutted on Saturday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past participle of “cut” is irregular and the same as the infinitive: “cut”.

ejercicios.frase: She got her son tidy his room.
respuestas: She got her son to tidy his room.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the variant with a person: get + person + to + infinitive. The clue is “got her son”, with get and a person as the object. With get you need “to” before the verb: “She got her son to tidy his room”. Without “to” it would be the structure with have, not with get.
ejercicios.traduccion: Consiguió que su hijo ordenara su habitación.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She got her son tidy his room.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: with get the person is followed by “to” + infinitive.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She got her son tidied his room.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past participle is only used when the object is a thing; here the son carries out the action: “to tidy”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She got to her son tidy his room.
errores_previstos.explicacion: “To” goes before the verb, not before the person.

ejercicios.frase: We had the roof repair after the storm.
respuestas: We had the roof repaired after the storm.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the structure have + object + past participle. The clue is “had the roof”, which already has have in the past and the object in place; what is wrong is the final verb, which is in the infinitive. After the object you need the past participle: “repaired”. The correct sentence is “We had the roof repaired after the storm”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After the object comes the past participle (repaired).
ejercicios.traduccion: Después de la tormenta nos arreglaron el tejado.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We had the roof repair after the storm.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: after the object comes the past participle “repaired”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We had repaired the roof after the storm.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is the past perfect (we had repaired): it would mean you repaired it yourselves.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We had the roof repairing after the storm.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The -ing form does not make the causative; you need the past participle.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence with have + object + past participle.
ejercicios.frase: A mechanic checked my brakes yesterday.
respuestas: I had my brakes checked yesterday.
I had my brakes checked by a mechanic yesterday.
Yesterday I had my brakes checked.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the structure have + object + past participle, which the card allows you to complete with by + person. The clue is “A mechanic checked my brakes”: another person did it as a service. It becomes “I had my brakes checked yesterday”, with the past “had” because the original is in the past. Variants with “by a mechanic” and with “Yesterday” at the beginning are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Someone else did it as a service: had + object + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ayer me revisaron los frenos (un mecánico).

errores_previstos.respuesta: I had checked my brakes yesterday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The object goes before the past participle; “had checked” is the past perfect and would mean you checked them yourself.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I checked my brakes yesterday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It would mean you checked the brakes yourself; the causative structure is missing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I have my brakes checked yesterday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: With “yesterday”, have must be in the past: “had”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I had a mechanic check my brakes yesterday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is correct English (have + person + bare infinitive), but the instructions ask for have + object + past participle: I had my brakes checked yesterday.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence with have + object + past participle.
ejercicios.frase: Someone broke into our flat last week. (our flat)
respuestas: We had our flat broken into last week.
Last week we had our flat broken into.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the use on the card for negative experiences: have + object + past participle. The clue is “Someone broke into our flat”, a misfortune suffered, and the words in brackets, “our flat”, which must be the object. The verb is the phrasal verb “break into” (to enter in order to steal), so the past participle keeps its preposition: “broken into”. The result is “We had our flat broken into last week”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Negative experience: have + object + past participle (with the preposition of the phrasal verb).
ejercicios.traduccion: La semana pasada nos entraron a robar en el piso.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We had our flat broken last week.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The preposition of the phrasal verb is missing: “broken into”. “Broken” alone would only mean the flat was broken.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We had broken into our flat last week.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It would mean you broke into your own flat; the object goes before the past participle.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We had our flat broke into last week.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The past participle of “break” is “broken”, not “broke” (which is the past simple).

ejercicios.enunciado: Make the question in the past simple.
respuestas: Did you have the documents translated?
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule on the card: causative have behaves like a normal verb and forms questions and negatives with do. The clue is “You had…”, in the past simple, so the question takes “Did” and have goes back to the base form. The rest does not change: “Did you have the documents translated?”. “Had” is not inverted with the subject, because here have is not an auxiliary.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Causative have forms questions with do/did.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¿Te tradujeron los documentos? (¿Mandaste traducir los documentos?)

errores_previstos.respuesta: Had you the documents translated?
errores_previstos.explicacion: Causative have is not inverted with the subject: it forms the question with “did”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Did you had the documents translated?
errores_previstos.explicacion: After “did” the verb goes back to the base form: “have”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Did you have translated the documents?
errores_previstos.explicacion: The object “the documents” goes before the past participle.

respuestas: we're having a new kitchen fitted
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the structure have + object + past participle with have in the continuous, as shown on the card (“I'm having…”). The clue is “we're having”, which opens the sentence, and the past participle “fitted” (installed), which goes at the end. In the middle goes the object with its adjectives: “a new kitchen”. “To fit a kitchen” is to install a kitchen.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Have (in the continuous) + object + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Nos están poniendo una cocina nueva.

errores_previstos.respuesta: we're having fitted a new kitchen
errores_previstos.explicacion: The object “a new kitchen” goes before the past participle “fitted”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: we're having a kitchen new fitted
errores_previstos.explicacion: In English the adjective goes before the noun: “a new kitchen”.

respuestas: I'll have my assistant call you
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the variant from the table have + person + bare infinitive, for asking someone to do something. The clue is “I'll have”: the verb is have and the person, “my assistant”, will be the one who carries out the action. After that comes “call” without to and the object “you”. It is a very frequent formula in professional language.
ejercicios.traduccion: Le diré a mi ayudante que te llame.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'll have you call my assistant
errores_previstos.explicacion: It reverses who does what: it would mean you will call my assistant.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'll have call my assistant you
errores_previstos.explicacion: The person who carries out the action goes right after have: “have my assistant call you”.

descripcion_larga_es: The causative with have or get (have + object + past participle) shows that another person does something for us, usually because we arrange or pay for it: I had my hair cut. It is also used to talk about something bad that happened to us (I had my phone stolen). It is difficult because Spanish says “me corté el pelo” even if the hairdresser did it, and because the order is fixed and not very intuitive.

contexto.que_es: It is a construction in which the subject does not carry out the action but makes someone else do it: have/get + object + past participle (I had the car serviced). It has variants with a person: have + person + bare infinitive (I'll have my assistant call you) and get + person + to + infinitive (I got him to help me). Have can be conjugated in any tense.
contexto.por_que_importa: It is the natural way to talk about everyday services: the hairdresser's, repairs, check-ups, translations. Without it, English understands that you did it yourself: “I cut my hair” means you cut your hair yourself. In B2-level exams and above it is a classic sentence-transformation structure.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When you talk about services you arrange (having your hair cut, the car repaired, the house painted), about what you get others to do, and about misfortunes (thefts, damage). The signal is usually a professional or a service in the context (hairdresser's, mechanic) or damage suffered. Spanish speakers tend to use the verb directly (“I repaired my car”) or to mix up the order of the structure (“I had repaired my car”, which is a different tense).
